Binding for every project of this folder. Fixed 2026-10-24 by the Round 4 run 6 coordinator, before drafting project 1
(the Hittite elimination rituals of Ašḫella, Uḫḫamuwa, Puliša and Ambazzi). The Hittite language tables are in
../חוקים-ובריתות/renderings.md §7 and §H2–§H9 (names, reserved and gated words, formulas, traps, the law corpus's
animals, purity terms and šipant-): they bind these rituals too, and tools/hittite_tools.py reads the H-tables of both
files. The translator brief is ../חוקים-ובריתות/translator-brief--hittite.md.

The danger specific to this corpus. Leviticus 14 and 16 are the natural Hebrew for a rite that loads evil on an
animal and sends it away: שָׂעִיר, עֲזָאזֵל, כִּפֶּר, נָשָׂא עָוֹן, שִׁלַּח, הַמִּדְבָּרָה, אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה,
סָמַךְ, הִתְוַדָּה, גּוֹרָל, שְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת, אֵזֹב, צִפֹּר חַיָּה, עַל פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה. A translator who reaches for
them makes Ašḫella sound like Aaron. So the words whose Hittite counterpart exists are gated to it (שִׁלַּח =
tarna-, נָשָׂא = peda-, צִפּוֹר = MUŠEN, אֶרֶז = ERIN, טִהֵר = parkunu-, טֻמְאָה = papratar, מַחֲנֶה =
KARAŠ, תַּיִשׁ = MÁŠ.GAL, עַכְבָּר = PÉŠ, מַגֵּפָה = ÚŠ), and the rest are reserved (never in a line):
שָׂעִיר, עֲזָאזֵל, the root כפר, מִדְבָּר, עָוֹן, פֶּשַׁע, סָמַךְ, הִתְוַדָּה, גּוֹרָל, תּוֹלַעַת, אֵזוֹב, זָבַח.
What is then the same, and what differs (the enemy's land against the wilderness; a woman, a ram, a bull, a mouse
against a goat; the god of the enemy against Azazel), appears in the apparatus as the finding.

R1. Ritual terms (Hittite → Hebrew)

Hittite (Sumerogram / Akkadogram) Hebrew Rejected Echo Reason
UMMA X "thus (says) X" (the opening) כֹּה (אוֹמֵר) X (F10) כֹּה אָמַר (the prophets' messenger formula adds a verb the Akkadogram lacks) [equivalent] ↔ כֹּה אָמַר
SISKUR / SÍSKUR (mukeššar, malteššar) "ritual" טֶקֶס קָרְבָּן
ÚŠ (ḫenkan) "plague, (the) death" מַגֵּפָה (gated) דֶּבֶר (a trap: "word, thing") [equivalent] ↔ כִּי מַגֵּפָה אַחַת לְכֻלָּם (שמואל א ו:ד)
KARAŠ "army camp"; EN.MEŠ KARAŠ "the lords of the camp" מַחֲנֶה (gated); אֲדוֹנֵי הַמַּחֲנֶה [equivalent] ↔ יָבוֹא אֶל הַמַּחֲנֶה (ויקרא טז:כו)
KUR LÚ.KÚR "the enemy's land"; DINGIR LÚ.KÚR / kururaš DINGIR-LUM "the enemy's god" אֶרֶץ הָאוֹיֵב; אֵל הָאוֹיֵב אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה, מִדְבָּר (reserved) [divergence] ↔ אֶל אֶרֶץ גְּזֵרָה (ויקרא טז:כב) The evil is sent back to where it came from, to a god who sent it: the finding.
gimra- "the open country" הַבָּר שָׂדֶה (that is A.ŠÀ), מִדְבָּר [equivalent] ↔ עַל פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה (ויקרא יד:ז)
idālu- "evil" (adj.), idālu (n.) רַע; הָרָעָה עָוֹן, חַטָּאת [divergence] ↔ אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (ויקרא טז:כא) The Hittite evil is a substance, not a guilt.
papratar "impurity"; ḫurtai- "curse"; lingai- "oath"; eš(ḫ)ar "blood(shed)"; waštul "sin" טֻמְאָה (gated); קְלָלָה; שְׁבוּעָה (gated); דָּם; חֵטְא (gated)
tarna- (arḫa / parā tarna-) "let go, release" שִׁלַּח (gated) (שִׁלַּח הָלְאָה, שִׁלַּח הַחוּצָה); but anda tarna- "let in, put in" = הִכְנִיס (Sub4, R1a) [equivalent] ↔ וְשִׁלַּח אֶת הַצִּפֹּר הַחַיָּה עַל פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה (ויקרא יד:ז); וְשִׁלַּח אֶת הַשָּׂעִיר בַּמִּדְבָּר (ויקרא טז:כב) One verb for one verb.
penna- (arḫa penna-) "drive (away)"; unna- "drive (hither)" הִסִּיעַ (הִסִּיעַ הָלְאָה); נָהַג (corrected by Sub4: the Laws' precedent, HL1 457 / 407, R1a) גֵּרַשׁ, שִׁלַּח ↔ וַיַּסַּע כַּצֹּאן עַמּוֹ (תהלים עח:נב), in the apparatus
peda- "carry, take (away)"; uda- "bring"; karp- "lift" נָשָׂא (gated); הֵבִיא; הֵרִים [equivalent] ↔ וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר עָלָיו (ויקרא טז:כב)
nai- "turn, send"; nāišḫut "turn (yourself)!" הִפְנָה; פְּנֵה! שָׁלַח שלח stays tarna-'s.
ḫuittiya- "draw, pull"; SUD-ru "let it be drawn" מָשַׁךְ; יִמָּשֵׁךְ
dai- "put, place"; dā- "take" (both dāi in the 3sg: decide by context, say so) שָׂם (decided by Sub4, 2026-10-30, with the Laws and IN, §7.10 of the law file: הִנִּיחַ is dala- / dāliya- "leave"); לָקַח הִנִּיחַ (the coordinator's first choice, dropped) [equivalent] לָקַח ↔ וְלָקַח לַמִּטַּהֵר (ויקרא יד:ד)
šipant- "offer (by libation or slaughter)"; ḫuek- "slaughter"; warnu- "burn"; ed- / eku- "eat" / "drink" הִקְרִיב (gated; a note at the first occurrence: the verb is "to libate") ; שָׁחַט (gated); שָׂרַף; אָכַל / שָׁתָה זָבַח, נִסֵּךְ (open: the translator may propose נִסֵּךְ for a real libation of liquid)
UDU.ŠIR "breeding ram"; UDU.NÍTA "male sheep"; GU₄.MAḪ "bull"; MÁŠ.GAL "he-goat"; PÉŠ.TUR "little mouse"; MUŠEN "bird"; MUNUS "woman"; unuwant- "adorned" אַיִל; כֶּבֶשׂ; פַּר; תַּיִשׁ (gated); עַכְבָּר קָטָן (gated); צִפּוֹר (gated); אִשָּׁה; מְקֻשֶּׁטֶת שָׂעִיר (reserved) [divergence] ↔ שְׁנֵי שְׂעִירֵי עִזִּים (ויקרא טז:ה); עַכְבְּרֵי זָהָב (שמואל א ו:ד) The law table (../חוקים-ובריתות/renderings.md §7.1) for the other animals.
SÍG "wool"; SA₅ "red"; ZA.GÌN "blue (wool)"; SIG₇ "green, yellow"; GE₆ "black"; BABBAR "white"; NA₄ ZA.GÌN "lapis"; NA₄ GUG "carnelian"; GUŠKIN; KÙ.BABBAR; AN.BAR "iron"; ZABAR "bronze"; NAGGA "tin" צֶמֶר; אָדֹם; כָּחֹל; יָרֹק; שָׁחֹר; לָבָן; אֶבֶן סַפִּיר (§6.7 harmonized uqnû); אֹדֶם; זָהָב; כֶּסֶף; בַּרְזֶל; אָרָד (vocalized; Akk. siparru: open); בְּדִיל (MAL annaku) שְׁנִי, תּוֹלַעַת, זְהוֹרִית, תְּכֵלֶת [divergence] ↔ וּשְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת (ויקרא יד:ד)
NINDA.GUR₄.RA "thick bread"; NINDA "bread"; KAŠ "beer"; GEŠTIN "wine"; Ì "oil, fat"; LÀL "honey"; išna- "dough"; DUG ḫuppar "bowl" לֶחֶם עָבֶה; לֶחֶם; שֵׁכָר (§6.7 kaš); יַיִן; שֶׁמֶן; דְּבַשׁ; בָּצֵק; קְעָרָה
GIŠ ERIN "cedar"; GIŠ laḫḫurnuzzi "foliage, leafy branches"; GIŠ.ŠINIG "tamarisk" אֶרֶז (gated); עַלְוָה; אֵשֶׁל אֵזוֹב (reserved) [equivalent] ↔ וְעֵץ אֶרֶז (ויקרא יד:ד)
kāša, kāšma "here (is), behold" הִנֵּה "Here is an adorned woman for you" (Ašḫella): the address to the god.
arḫa; parā; anda; šer; katta; EGIR-pa; peran הָלְאָה; הַחוּצָה / קָדִימָה; פְּנִימָה; עַל; מַטָּה; בַּחֲזָרָה; לִפְנֵי Preverbs: render where they carry meaning (guidelines §6.3 on the ventive).
-wa(r) (the quotative particle) quotation marks only לֵאמֹר
TI-tar (ḫuišwatar) "life"; MU.ḪI.A GÍD.DA "long years"; innarawatar "vigour"; aššul "well-being, favour" חַיִּים; שָׁנִים אֲרֻכּוֹת; translator (עוֹז is Ugaritic ʿz's); translator (not שָׁלוֹם) הֶאֱרִיךְ יָמִים
ḪUR.SAG.MEŠ "mountains"; ḫallu- "deep"; parku- "high"; dalugi- "long" הָרִים; עָמֹק; גָּבֹהַּ; אָרֹךְ Ambazzi: the mouse takes the evil "to the high mountains, the deep valleys, the long roads".

R1a. Checked against the transliteration before the first line (Round 4 run 6 Sub4, 2026-10-30)

Every row of R1 was checked against the five HPM composites (AS, UH, PU, AM, AM2: 481 clauses). Corrections and additions,
binding for the translator unless it proposes otherwise with a reason:

  • tarna-: "release" (שִׁלַּח) only with arḫa / parā: the mouse let go (AM 41, 87, 168, 214), AS 53. anda tarna-
    "let in, put in" is another act: the wool threads twisted together (AS 10, UH 6), the blood let into the cup (AM 234), "do
    not let the evil in" (AM 227) = הִכְנִיס (never שִׁלַּח there: the gate cannot see the preverb, the translator must).
  • penna- "drive (away)" = הִסִּיעַ and unna- "drive (hither)" = נָהַג (the Laws: HL1 457 יסיע, 407 ינהג;
    IN 7.1, 19.2): R1's נָהַג for penna- is corrected. AS 20, 34, 43, 77, 90; UH 9, 18; AM 88 penna-; AS 75, 87; UH 5, 12, 27;
    PU 28 unna-.
  • dai- "put" = שָׂם (the Laws and IN, the Sub2 ruling of the law file §7.10; הִנִּיחַ belongs to dala-). The rituals'
    dāi is very often dai- "puts" (AM 14, 19, 51, 94, 100, 103–105 …) and sometimes dā- "takes" (AS 60, 62; AM 15, 18, 36,
    42): decide each by context and say which in the פירוק. tiyanzi / tianzi (AS 24, 79) is the 3pl of dai-.
  • The hand-placing: AS 24 ANA UDU.ŠIR{ḪI.A} EN{MEŠ} KARAŠ QĀTĪ=ŠUNU parā tiyanzi "the lords of the camp put their hands
    forth on the rams" = שָׂמִים … אֶת יְדֵיהֶם (dai- + parā); סָמַךְ is reserved (Lev 16:21): the comparison is the
    apparatus's.
  • The animals as the text has them: AS's rams are UDU.ŠIR אַיִל ★ (always vocalized, trap); Uḫḫamuwa's crowned animal
    is UDU.NÍTA כֶּבֶשׂ, a male sheep, not a ram     (the plan's "crowned ram" is the literature's); UDU.'SÍG+MUNUS' (AS 87–92)
    the ewe רָחֵל; UDU.ÁŠ.MUNUS.GÀR (PU 28, 47) כִּבְשָׂה (HL1); GU₄.MAḪ פַּר; MÁŠ.GAL תַּיִשׁ; MÁŠ.ŠIR (AM 232)
    licensed for תַּיִשׁ too (the translator qualifies it); UZ₆ (AM 89, 95) עֵז ★ (trap); ŠAḪ חֲזִיר; PÉŠ.TUR עַכְבָּר קָטָן; UDU שֶׂה (pl. צֹאן). There is no MUŠEN and no cedar (ERIN) in these five texts: the bird and the cedar of
    Lev 14 are [absent] here (the coloured wool and the "Babylon stone" are their nearest things).
  • KILĪLU "wreath, crown" (UH 7) = עֲטָרָה; ḫaršanallai- "crown, wreathe" (UH 8) = עִטֵּר, ptcp. (UH 12, 18)
    מְעֻטָּר; unuwant- "adorned" = מְקֻשָּׁט / מְקֻשֶּׁטֶת (AS 22, 32; PU 21, 23, 43, 47).
  • ÚŠ and ḫenkan (UH 15) "plague, death" = מַגֵּפָה both; akkiškittari / akkiškizzi "(people) keep dying"
    (UH 2, AS 105) = מֵתִים (a verb: never מגפה).
  • The plague's god (F17): kuiš=wa (=kan) DINGIR-LUM kī ÚŠ-kan iyat "whichever god made this plague" (AS 17, 26, 81; UH 11,
    15; PU 42) = "אֵיזֶה אֵל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אֶת הַמַּגֵּפָה הַזֹּאת (iyan ḫarzi: עָשָׂה, the perfect noted; UH 11 אֵיזֶה אֵל שֶׁל אֶרֶץ הָאוֹיֵב אֲשֶׁר …; UH 15 וְאַתָּה, אֵיזֶה אֵל אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתָ …); also AS 16 "אֵיזֶה אֵל אֲשֶׁר …. The indefinite
    kuiški DINGIR-LUM (UH 3, PU 4, 20) = אֵיזֶשֶׁהוּ אֵל / אֵל כָּלְשֶׁהוּ (the translator fixes one). kururaš "of
    enmity, of the enemy" = שֶׁל אוֹיֵב (the Laws: kururi KUR-e ארץ אויב); KUR LÚ.KÚR = אֶרֶץ הָאוֹיֵב.
  • The turn in favour (F18): aššuli (anda) nai- (AS 84; UH 17, 26; PU 24, 46) = בְּטוֹבָה פָּנָה (aššul "well-being,
    favour" = טוֹבָה: שָׁלוֹם is takšul's); nāišḫut פְּנֵה!, neyāru יִפָּנֶה. takšul- "peace, accord" = שָׁלוֹם
    (UH 12 takšulanni לְשָׁלוֹם), takšulai- "make peace" = עָשָׂה שָׁלוֹם (UH 14, 16), takšulant- (AS 83) בְּשָׁלוֹם
    (with ēšdu יִהְיֶה).
  • The dawn (F19): INA UD.n.KAM mān lukkatta karūwariwar ḫūdak (AS 42, 74, 87) = בַּיּוֹם הַ־n, כְּשֶׁעוֹלֶה הַשַּׁחַר, בְּהַשְׁכָּמָה, מִיָּד (lukkatt- שַׁחַר, IN; AS 20 lukkatti וּבַשַּׁחַר); AS 5 UD.KAM-az nekuz meḫūni זְמַן הָעֶרֶב
    (IN nekuz meḫur).
  • kāša (kāšma) "here, behold" = הִנֵּה (F21; AS 18, 27, 38, 39, 52, 54; UH 12; PU 21; AM 114); kāš "this one"
    (AM 40, 86, 167; PU 22, 25, 45) is the demonstrative: הַזֶּה.
  • kiššan memai = כָּךְ אוֹמֵר (the Laws' ruling §7.8); anda … memai "speaks over / into" = וְעָלָיו כָּךְ אוֹמְרִים
    / וְאֶל הָאִישׁ … כָּךְ אוֹמֵר (the translator fixes one per construction); memaḫḫi = אֲנִי אוֹמֶרֶת in Ambazzi (a woman,
    {f}), אֲנִי אוֹמֵר in Ašḫella; AM2 tezzi (tar-) = אוֹמֶרֶת (a split noted with HL1 tar- אמורה).
  • The colours (AS 10; UH 6; PU 32, 34): SÍG BABBAR צֶמֶר לָבָן ★ (unvocalized לבן = Laban, "to a son": trap), SA₅ אָדֹם
    ★ (plene אדום = Edom: trap), SIG₇.SIG₇ יָרֹק, ZA.GÌN (wool) כָּחֹל, GE₆ שָׁחֹר (GE₆ "night" לַיְלָה, IN: the sign's two
    words); PU 34's verbs ēšḫarwaḫḫ- "make blood-red", ḫaḫlaḫḫ- "make yellow-green", dankuwaḫḫ- "make dark" keep the colour
    roots (הֶאְדִּים, הוֹרִיק, הִשְׁחִיר). The stones (AM 113, 190, 252, 254): NA₄ ZA.GÌN סַפִּיר (§6.7, a note), NA₄ GUG
    אֹדֶם ★, NA₄ KÁ.DINGIR.RA אֶבֶן־בָּבֶל, the unknown lullūri, TI, barašḫa transliterated and vocalized (בַּרַשְׁחָה:
    never the string בראש); AN.BAR בַּרְזֶל, NAGGA בְּדִיל, URUDU נְחֹשֶׁת, ZABAR אָרָד (HL2), KÙ.BABBAR כֶּסֶף, GUŠKIN
    זָהָב.

    (UH 32) as HL2 קֵבָה? / the translator.

    on hand and foot, the mouse (34–40, 80–86, 160–167; AM2 18–21); "take him, we give you another to eat" (42–44, 88–89,
